summary: Adds columns after the last column that holds data.
description: Pass a sheet and the whole sheet is examined; pass a range and only the cells inside it are, which is how data further down the sheet is kept from pushing the write to the right. A range also decides the rows written on — the sheet always starts at row 1.

The values are a matrix of rows: one array per row, all of the same length. Nothing is overwritten — the write starts one column past the last one holding data, and `0` and `false` count as data. The sheet gains columns when it is too narrow for the result.
A cell whose text starts with `=` is written as a formula, not as text — the same rule the editor follows.

params.target: The sheet to append to, or the range to append within.
params.values: A matrix of rows: one array per row, all of the same length.
params.options: `afterFrozenColumns` starts the write past the frozen columns when the data ends before them.

returns: the sheet, so calls can be chained.

throws.InvalidSheetException: the first argument is neither a sheet nor a range.
throws.TypeError: the values are not a matrix with rows of equal length.
